xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4843: Phone app: native push provider that seals notifications to each phone

plan.title: Phone app: native push provider that seals notifications to each phone
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The phone app (epic PAN-4823) needs needs-you notifications while it is closed. Native push must go through Apple and Google, and the machine must not hold APNs or FCM credentials, so the machine has to hand each notification to the overdeck.ai directory. The directory must never see the content. Today needs-you push has only the Web Push and ntfy providers.
narratives.Proposal: Add a third PushProvider, 'native', in src/lib/push/native-provider.ts. For each active phone access-token record with a push key, it builds the PhonePushPayload JSON (new contracts type), trims it to PUSH_PLAINTEXT_MAX_BYTES (2,256), seals it with crypto_box_seal (new sealTo in sealed-box.ts) to that phone's push key, and sends a push frame through the directory client, waiting up to 10 s for push-result. The provider reaches the directory through a lazy port (currentDirectoryClient) because the push service starts before the directory client exists. GET /api/push/status gains native { phones, directoryOnline } and Settings shows 'Overdeck app: N phones'. Docs gain additive sentences.
narratives.NonGoals:
- The directory side: decoding push, APNs/FCM delivery, directory rate limiting (PAN-4830, W-CON3)
- The phone side: NSE / FirebaseMessagingService decryption and the tests/fixtures/phone-push fixture generator (W-IOS1, W-AND1), Live Activity push-activity frames (W-IOS2)
- Changing dispatcher stats, the 6-per-minute limit, dedup, or how Web Push and ntfy send
- Correlating directory error frames to push requests
- Any change to anywhere-boot.ts or directory-client.ts
- New HTTP routes, new config keys, or a per-phone notification list in Settings
- The full phone-app documentation (configuration/phone-app.mdx, CONNECT-SERVICE and ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE sections), owned by PAN-4842 (W-DOC)

autoDecisions.summary: Trim the plaintext to PUSH_PLAINTEXT_MAX_BYTES (2,256), not the epic's 2,900
autoDecisions.rationale: 2,900 bytes seal to 3,932 base64 characters, which the PUSH_SEALED_MAX_CHARS (3,072) contract cap refuses; the 2026-11-03 issue comment and PAN-4828 D-3 direct this issue to the exported constant.

autoDecisions.summary: Pass a lazy currentDirectoryClient getter from needs-you-push-service.ts instead of injecting a port in anywhere-boot.ts
autoDecisions.rationale: main.ts:224 voids startAnywhere and main.ts:277 starts the push service synchronously, so the directory client can be null when defaultProviders() runs; a getter resolved per call is required and the existing seam already provides it.

autoDecisions.summary: Map no_registration and unknown_client to the existing 'skipped' reason and make the Send test toast ignore skipped outcomes; leave dispatcher stats unchanged
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic says these are not operator errors; 'skipped' is the existing not-attempted reason, and changing dispatcher accounting would alter Web Push behaviour outside this issue while PushPanel does not display stats.

autoDecisions.summary: Seal notification.title (the full Web Push title), not publicTitle
autoDecisions.rationale: The payload is end-to-end encrypted to the phone, the same trust level as Web Push, which already sends title.
It is the wire format W-APP1, W-IOS1 and W-AND1 decode; connect.ts already holds the push frame and stays type-only; the plan stays at 6 subsystems.

autoDecisions.summary: Directory missing or offline yields a per-phone transient 'directory-offline' outcome instead of an empty list
autoDecisions.rationale: A paired phone that cannot be reached is a real delivery failure the operator should see on Send test, unlike ntfy's unconfigured state.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs change only sentences that would become false plus one provider section/paragraph
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-4842 (W-DOC) owns the full phone-app docs; PAN-4828 D-8 set the same pattern to avoid conflicting edits.

Update the file header to say it seals phone pushes as well as opening inbox events. New test file src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/sealed-box.test.ts builds key pairs with sodium-native crypto_box_seed_keypair (pattern: tests/unit/services/connect/seal-interop.test.ts).

narrative.Action: PRD W-3 / D-3 / D-4. Create src/lib/push/native-provider.ts with pure exports: buildPhonePushPayload(n, machine) (title = n.title, never publicTitle), fitPhonePushPayload(p) implementing the D-4 rule exactly (size = Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(p),'utf8'); cut by code points via Array.from; binary search largest k with body = prefix + '…'; then title with body ''; else return null; url/tag/machine/kind/issueId/ts never altered; cap imported as PUSH_PLAINTEXT_MAX_BYTES from @overdeck/contracts, never hard-coded 2256 or 2900), and pushCollapseId(tag) = sha256 hex first 32 chars. File header per PRD. Tests in tests/unit/lib/push/native-provider.test.ts, describe 'phone push payload (PAN-4843)', covering every W-3 test bullet.

items.title: Given a 5,000-byte ASCII body, fitPhonePushPayload returns a payload of at most 2,256 UTF-8 JSON bytes whose body ends with '…' and whose url, tag and machine are unchanged
Given a body of 3,000 '😀' characters or 2,000 '"' characters, the trimmed payload stays at most 2,256 bytes and contains no lone surrogate
Given a 3,000-character title, fitPhonePushPayload returns body '' and a title ending with '…'; given a 3,000-character url it returns null
pushCollapseId('auq:toolu_01') returns the first 32 lowercase hex characters of the sha256 hex digest
Send sealed push frames per phone with createNativePushProvider

narrative.Action: PRD W-4 / D-2 / D-5 / D-8. In src/lib/push/native-provider.ts export NATIVE_PUSH_RESULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000, the PushDirectoryPort interface (isOnline, send(MachineToDirectoryFrame): boolean, on('push-result', handler) => off), nativePushPhones() (active phone records from listActiveRecordsOfKind('phone') that have clientId and pushKey), and createNativePushProvider({ directory, listPhones?, environmentId?, randomRequestId? }). The directory getter is resolved on every hasTargets()/send() call (never captured). name 'native'; hasTargets = phones > 0 && port online. send(): [] when no phones; fit payload once; per phone in Promise.allSettled: directory-offline check, sealTo(pushKey) base64 (seal-failed on throw), subscribe push-result filtered by requestId BEFORE port.send, 10 s setTimeout, map every outcome per the D-5 table with target 'native:<clientId>', always clear timer and unsubscribe. Urgency via webPushUrgency from ./webpush-provider.js. Import nothing from src/dashboard/server. Logs carry only the first 8 chars of clientId and the detail; skip logging 'skipped'. Tests per W-4 using a fake port and vi.useFakeTimers/advanceTimersByTimeAsync.

items.title: Given two phones, when send(question) runs, the port receives one push frame per clientId whose sealed field opens with openSealed only under that phone's key pair to buildPhonePushPayload(n, 'env-1')

Each push frame carries urgency 'high' for question and 'normal' for finished, collapseId equal to pushCollapseId(tag), a 32-hex requestId, and sealed.length at most PUSH_SEALED_MAX_CHARS (a 2,256-byte plaintext produces exactly 3,072 characters)
push-result errors no_registration and unknown_client return reason 'skipped', rate_limited and delivery_failed return 'transient' with the error as detail, and ok:true returns ok
When no push-result arrives, after advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10_000) the outcome is transient/timeout and the port holds no push-result handler
When the directory getter returns null, isOnline is false, or send returns false, the outcome is transient/directory-offline without waiting, and hasTargets returns false
